provider.response_format: json_schema wrapper {name, schema, strict} (raw schema is rejected with 422 despite the docs)
provider.transport_retry_policy: a request that was never sent (its connection, proxy tunnel or TLS handshake failed before any byte of it was written) closes its reservation at a known $0 and is sent again at most 2 times after 2/6 s, each attempt under a new reservation, each recorded and counted against the call cap; a request whose bytes were written is never sent again (its reservation stays committed)
provider.reservation_policy: the USD reservation is journaled durably (fsync) and read back before dispatch, after any cut journal tail has been terminated with a journal_repair record; if it cannot be, the request is not sent and the run stops paid calls
provider.metering_policy: an HTTP 200 whose usage cannot price the generation (missing, empty, partial or malformed counters) keeps its reservation unsettled and stops further paid calls of the run pending reconciliation; explicit zero counters settle as 0
provider.answer_policy: HTTP 4xx: a definite rejection at a known $0; HTTP 5xx or a failure after the request was written: uncertain, the reservation stays committed, nothing is sent again and the run stops for reconciliation
provider.call_cap_policy: at most 22 model calls per run (failed calls and retries count); the call that would exceed it is refused before dispatch

executor.journal_policy: every operation is journaled as PENDING (fsync, read back) before its spawn is sent and its accepted id before the first poll; when either fails nothing further is dispatched and the run halts for reconciliation
executor.answer_policy: a spawn answered HTTP 4xx is REJECTED; HTTP 5xx, a 2xx without an operation id or a failure after the spawn was written is UNCERTAIN and halts the run; polls are retried (bounded) and an accepted operation whose outcome is not read is ACCEPTED_UNREAD; nothing is sent after the run halts
executor.transport: base64 stdin JSON job -> guest runner (root); sealed tests run per-test as uid 65534
executor.retry_policy: GET and DELETE retried on any transport failure (at most 4 times); a spawn sent again only when the attempt failed before any byte of it was written (at most 2 times); an uncertain spawn is never sent again; accepted operation ids are journaled before polling

task.title: Behaviour-preserving refactor of kvparse.parser
task.statement: Refactor kvparse/parser.py without changing any behaviour. Two changes are requested. (1) parse_line(line) must be rewritten without the hand-rolled index loops: split the line at the first '=' with str.partition, strip the key and the value, raise ValueError when there is no '=' or the stripped key is empty, and remove one pair of matching surrounding quotes (both ends '"' or both ends "'") from a stripped value of length two or more; the function must not contain a 'while' loop. (2) Extract the detection of ignorable lines into a module-level function _is_ignorable(line) -> bool in kvparse/parser.py that returns True exactly when the stripped line is empty or starts with '#' or ';', and make parse use it. The observable behaviour of parse and parse_line must stay byte-for-byte identical for every str input: the same return values, the same exception types in the same situations (TypeError for non-string input to parse, ValueError for a malformed line), later duplicate keys still win, and quotes are removed only when the stripped value starts and ends with the same quote character (a value like '"x\'' keeps both characters; a lone '"' is kept). Exception messages are not prescribed. parse keeps raising TypeError for non-string input; what parse_line does with a non-string argument (for example a list or a mapping) is unspecified and must not be tested, because the required use of str.partition changes it. Keep the public names parse and parse_line exported from kvparse, do not modify the tests, and keep the existing suite passing.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing tests' bodies changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant, with every result structurally sound and bound to its nonce); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception, whatever its origin, is never overridden (only a test the supervisor killed at its timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

A mutant counts as killed only when a sealed test failed with an authentic child result under a structurally sound supervisor run; lost, forged, incomplete, non-isolated, crashed or timed-out runs are unknown and excluded from the mutation score, and `attest check` recomputes the classification from the raw results.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.

Once an operation's outcome is uncertain, or a record of the run cannot be made durable, the run sends nothing further and ends ERROR with every unsettled operation listed under reconciliation; such operations are settled by a human against the providers' records, never by sending them again. Operations being polled in parallel when the run stops are not read further and are listed too.

manifest.json lists the sha256 of every artifact and `python -m attest check <run dir or zip>` recomputes digests, the sealed and adversarial bindings from verify_raw.json and the gate-to-verdict rule offline; it cannot re-execute the sandbox runs themselves.

evidence_protocol.note: a VERIFIED bundle of this protocol carries every gate with its raw supervisor result, every evaluated mutant's raw result, the base and mutant evidence of any validated correction, the contract audit and the ledger; an INFEASIBLE bundle carries the executed witness, its digest, output and operation, its analysis in the constrained witness language and copies of the repository files that analysis resolved call origins through; every bundle carries the reconciliation record, and one that lists an operation whose outcome is unknown, or whose run halted, is ERROR; a bundle without this field is historical and is checked for internal consistency only

reconciliation.rule: once an operation's outcome is uncertain (a request that may have been executed and whose answer is unknown, an accepted operation whose outcome was not read, an answer that could not be priced) or a record of the run could not be made durable, the run sends nothing further: no model call, no sandbox operation, no poll; it ends ERROR with every such operation listed here with the read-only check that settles it, and none of them is ever sent again
